claims.text: Applying a thin, oxidation-resistant coating to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr improves its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The relevant initial material state is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast condition.
Coating material and deposition method mediate the effect of the intervention.
The coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion reduces oxide-layer formation.
Coating will reduce the oxidation rate relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Coating will increase time-to-pesting relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating can preserve useful room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical performance.
The hypothesis is applicable in air from 800 to 1000 °C for exposure times of 5 to 100 hours under low-to-moderate stress.

contradictions.description: The predicted benefit is an increased time-to-pesting, but the falsification rule describes lack of improvement as time-to-pesting not being significantly reduced. Reduction would indicate earlier pesting and is the opposite of the predicted direction.
